stories.title: Europe battles wildfires and braces for another summer heatwave
stories.summary: As well as drought, Europe has also been battling wildfires this summer. Firefighters this week are struggling to control a rapidly expanding wildfire in southwestern Spain that has forced the evacuation of around 800 people. For more on that topic, FRANCE 24's Nadia Massih is joined by Alexander Held, Senior Fire Management Expert at the European Forest Institute.

stories.title: ‘Real mummy’s curse’: health warning over growing trade in mummified human remains
stories.summary: Academic paper says often illicit trade exposes enthusiasts – and postal workers handling items – to serious risks A growing global trade in mummified human remains has been described by academics as “a real mummy’s curse” that poses a serious health risk to its enthusiasts and the postal services they use. Research into the secretive buying and selling of centuries-old human body parts including hands, feet and heads found alarming risks from dormant microorganisms and the toxic materials used to preserve the remains. stories.title: Miscarriages triple, healthcare access worsens… the nightmare for pregnant women in Gaza
stories.summary: With over 3,950 cases recorded by the ministry of health in Gaza, the number of miscarriages between January and June has tripled compared with the previous six months. During this period, there was approximately one miscarriage for every five live births. The Observers team spoke with two OBGYN doctors in Gaza.

stories.title: French pastry chef crowned world's best aims 'to be world champion every day'
stories.summary: For the world's newly crowned best pastry chef Frenchman Benoit Castel, pastry is less a matter of following recipes than listening to ingredients. In one of his many patisserie kitchens in Paris, he works alongside his team, tasting, testing and experimenting while remaining driven to try new things — from sourdough bread to anti-waste loaves and elaborate Christmas creations.

stories.title: Detained Malian journalist Ras Bath rejects charges as trial opens
stories.summary: The trial of Malian commentator Youssouf Bathily, known as Ras Bath, and activist Rose opened on August 10 before the Bamako Court of Appeal, with both denying accusations of criminal association and undermining state institutions.
stories.post: 📰 NEWS: Detained Malian journalist Ras Bath rejects charges as trial opens. The trial of Malian commentator Youssouf Bathily, known as Ras Bath, and activist Rose opened on August 10 before the Bamako Court of Appeal, with both denying. Source: Africanews English.
article_sentences: The trial of Malian commentator Youssouf Bathily, known as Ras Bath, and activist Rose opened on August 10 before the Bamako Court of Appeal, with both denying accusations of criminal association and undermining state institutions.
The first hearing focused largely on audio recordings presented by prosecutors as evidence.
Ras Bath, who has been in provisional detention for nearly three years, rejected the charges against him.
When asked in court whether he admitted to the accusations, he answered “No” and remained composed throughout the hearing.
Meanwhile, Rose told the court that her social media posts and public remarks were meant to alert the authorities to rising prices and the cost of basic goods, not to destabilize the institutions.
Prosecutors say the two were linked through repeated media appearances, including two interviews in which Ras Bath invited Rose onto his shows.
The defense disputes that interpretation and has asked for the audio recordings to be removed from the case.
Supporters gathered outside the court and chanted “Free Ras Bath” as the hearing ended.
The trial is due to resume on August 12.
